name: New Orleans café au lait
caffeine: From the coffee alone: chicory root carries no caffeine, and the hot milk adds none.

house.ask: Not printed on our menus: ask at lineup whether the bar will make one from our coffee with chicory and hot milk, and its price.

what: Dark roast coffee blended with roasted chicory root, brewed strong and poured with an equal measure of hot milk. Chicory gives a darker, more bitter cup with a full body; the milk softens it. Our printed New Orleans-style coffee with chicory is the cup it would start from.
taste: Roasty and smooth, with a gentle cocoa-like bitterness from the chicory, rounded and sweetened by the hot milk.

steps: Brew the chicory blend by drip or press at about 50 g per litre, since chicory brews strong.
Heat an equal measure of milk until it steams, about 149F (65C); never boil it.
Pour the hot coffee and milk into a warmed cup together, in equal parts.
Offer sugar and serve at once, while both are hot.
make.ratio: Equal parts strong chicory coffee and hot milk
make.dose: About 50 g chicory blend per litre; equal milk
make.time: Batch 4 to 8 minutes; sell within 30 to 60 minutes sealed
make.cup: Warmed cup or mug, 6 to 12 oz

serve: On a saucer, the handle towards the guest's right hand, sugar offered. It belongs beside dessert: our chicory coffee is the zero-proof pairing for six sweet plates, Bananas Foster among them.
story: Chicory stretched coffee in France during the blockades of the early 1800s, and New Orleans, a French city and a great coffee port, kept the habit. The city credits the Union blockade of 1861; tell that as tradition. A French Market coffee stand has poured it with chicory beside beignets since 1862.
guest: Chicory coffee with an equal measure of hot milk: roasty and smooth, with a soft, cocoa-like bitterness.
watch: Chicory has no caffeine, but the coffee does: never sell it as a decaf.
Boiled milk brings a skin and a cooked taste.
A guest who finds black chicory coffee bitter may prefer it with hot milk.

recall.prompt: How is a New Orleans café au lait made?
recall.answer: Coffee and chicory brewed strong, about 50 g per litre, poured in equal parts into a warmed cup with milk heated until it steams, never boiled. Roasty, smooth, softly bitter.

quiz.q: What does chicory bring to a New Orleans café au lait?
options: Sweetness and a hint of vanilla
quiz.explain: Roasted chicory root adds body, colour and a roasty, cocoa-like bitterness, with no caffeine of its own.

quiz.q: Why does a chicory blend take a lighter dose than straight coffee?
quiz.explain: Chicory gives up colour and body fast, so a blend brews strong at about 50 g per litre.

quiz.q: Which shortage does the city's own chicory story credit?
quiz.explain: The city tells the Union blockade from 1861, but France used chicory in the early 1800s first.
